question: What organ performs the respiratory and nutritional functions for a foetus?
explanation: The placenta acts as the lifeline for the foetus, handling gas exchange and nutrient transfer since the baby's organs are still immature. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h1)

question: Why does foetal circulation bypass the lungs?

options.A: The liver consumes all the oxygen before it reaches the chest
options.B: Blood pressure in the lungs is too low for oxygen exchange
options.C: The lungs are filled with fluid and do not oxygenate blood yet
options.D: The mother's lungs process all the oxygen required for the foetus

explanation: Foetal lungs are collapsed and filled with fluid, meaning gas exchange happens at the placenta instead. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h1)

question: Name the shunt that connects the pulmonary artery to the descending aorta.
explanation: The ductus arteriosus diverts blood from the pulmonary artery straight into the aorta, bypassing the lungs. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h2)

question: What is the primary function of the foramen ovale?

options.A: Draining deoxygenated blood back through the umbilical arteries
options.B: Connecting the umbilical vein directly to the inferior vena cava
options.C: Preventing blood from entering the developing liver tissues
options.D: Allowing blood to flow from the right atrium to the left atrium

explanation: The foramen ovale pushes blood straight from the right side of the heart to the left, bypassing the lungs. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h2)

question: Through which vessel does oxygenated blood travel from the placenta to the foetus?
explanation: The umbilical vein carries freshly oxygenated and nutrient-rich blood from the placenta straight into the foetal body. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h3)

question: Which foetal body part receives the highest concentration of oxygenated blood?
explanation: Routing blood through the foramen ovale straight to the aorta ensures the brain and upper body get the most oxygen. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h3)

question: How many umbilical arteries carry deoxygenated blood from the foetus back to the placenta?
explanation: The foetal umbilical cord contains two arteries carrying deoxygenated blood away and one vein bringing oxygenated blood in. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h4)

question: Where does the blood in the pulmonary trunk mostly go instead of the foetal lungs?

options.A: Through the umbilical vein back into the placental tissue
options.B: Through the foramen ovale into the left atrium
options.C: Through the ductus venosus into the inferior vena cava
options.D: Through the ductus arteriosus into the descending aorta

explanation: High pressure in the lungs forces blood in the pulmonary trunk to bypass them via the ductus arteriosus. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h4)

question: What event causes the foramen ovale to physically close at birth?

options.A: The first contraction of the left ventricle
options.B: Decreased body temperature of the baby
options.C: Increased pressure in the left atrium
options.D: The clamping of the umbilical cord

explanation: When the baby breathes and lung blood flow rises, pressure in the left atrium increases and seals the foramen ovale flap. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h5)

question: What triggers the functional closure of the ductus arteriosus after birth?

options.A: Increased pressure inside the right ventricle
options.B: The complete absence of circulating red blood cells
options.C: Rapid cooling of the newborn skin
options.D: High oxygen levels in the blood

explanation: The sudden surge of oxygen after the first breath causes the smooth muscle of the ductus arteriosus to constrict. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h5)

question: What condition occurs when the ductus arteriosus fails to close after birth?
explanation: A patent ductus arteriosus means the temporary foetal vessel remains open, allowing blood to flow abnormally between the aorta and pulmonary artery. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h6)

question: Why are preterm infants more likely to experience a persistent ductus arteriosus?

options.A: Their placenta remains attached inside the uterine cavity
options.B: Their livers produce too many clotting proteins too early
options.C: Their umbilical cords are cut much faster than full-term babies
options.D: Their blood vessels have lower sensitivity to high oxygen levels

explanation: Immature smooth muscle tissue in preterm infants does not constrict as effectively when exposed to newborn oxygen levels. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h6)
